name: Register a return for delivered order
description: Applies when a customer asks to return an item from a delivered order and receive a refund to a chosen payment method.
procedure:
- Look up the user by name and zip to authenticate, and confirm the order belongs to that user.
- Fetch order details and verify the order status is "delivered" and the requested item id appears in the order's items.
- Read the returns policy and compute days since delivery; confirm the item's category is inside its return window and it is not a clearance item.
- Confirm the reason is one of the allowed ones and the refund destination (e.g., a gift card) exists on the customer's account.
- Register the return with the item ids, order id, refund destination, and reason; report the resulting refund amount to the customer.
check: After registering, compare the refund amount in the tool response against the item price minus the restocking fee for the customer's membership tier, and confirm the refund transaction in payment_history went to the requested payment method.
known_bad: Registering a return for an item delivered more than the category's return window ago (e.g., an electronics item delivered 20 days earlier) succeeds in some systems; the window check in the procedure would have refused it, and the refund amount check cannot rescue an out-of-window return.

name: Exchange an item on a delivered order
description: Applies when a customer asks to exchange an item from a delivered order for a different variant of the same product, possibly paying or refunding the price difference.
procedure:
- Authenticate the customer and fetch their details; confirm the order belongs to them and its status is `delivered`.
- Read the exchange policy, then verify the return window for the item's category against `delivered_at` and the current timestamp (e.g. electronics 14, apparel 30, home 30 days).
- Fetch the product's variants and verify the requested new item is a variant of the **same product**, is `available`, and is **not** clearance.
- Compare prices: if the new variant is more expensive, charge the difference to a payment method on file (a gift card must cover it in full, otherwise refuse or use another method the customer accepts); if cheaper, refund the difference.
- Call the exchange action with the original item id, the new item id, the order id, and the chosen payment method.
check: Recompute the price difference from the order and product data (new variant price minus original item price) and confirm it matches the `exchange_price_difference` in the tool result, and that the tool result shows status changed and the correct `exchange_items`/`exchange_new_items`.
known_bad: Exchanging into a clearance or unavailable variant must not be executed: e.g. an exchange to a variant marked `clearance: true` or `available: false` fails the check because the procedure requires aborting before any exchange call is made.

name: Modify an item on a pending order
description: Applies when a customer asks to change an item on an order that is still in pending status to a different variant of the same product, paying or refunding the price difference.
procedure:
- Verify the user's identity and that the order belongs to them, then confirm the order status is still pending (modifications are not allowed once it ships).
- Look up the product and confirm the requested variant belongs to the same product, is available, and is not a clearance item.
- Compute the price difference as the new variant's price minus the current item's price (can be negative, meaning a refund).
- Settle the difference via the original payment method or a gift card; if using a gift card for an upcharge, confirm its balance covers the full difference.
- Confirm the plan and any charge with the customer, then call the modify-pending-order-items action with the old item id, new item id, order id, and payment method id.
- Report the resulting item and the charged or refunded amount to the customer.
check: After the modification, re-fetch the order and verify the item now shows the new variant's id, options and price, and that the payment history contains a transaction for the computed price difference on the chosen payment method; also recompute the difference from the two item prices to confirm the charged amount matches.
known_bad: Swapping an item for a same-product variant that is marked clearance or unavailable should be rejected before calling the modify action, so an order whose items are unchanged except for a charged price difference but whose new variant is clearance fails this check because the modification should never have been attempted.

name: Resolve an ambiguous timestamp
description: Applies when the current time is given as an opaque number with no stated unit or epoch and a deadline or return window must be checked against a calendar date.
procedure:
- Treat any explicit calendar date stated in the task (e.g. a stated "today" date) as authoritative; ignore the opaque number when the two conflict.
- If no explicit calendar date is given, list the plausible interpretations of the number (days since delivery, day of year, days since an epoch) and check each against the relevant window.
- Compute elapsed days from the order's delivered_at (or placed_at) to the authoritative date using the stated return window for the item category.
- If interpretations disagree and no authoritative date exists, do not take an irreversible action that depends on the window; state the ambiguity and ask or refuse.
check: Recompute the elapsed days from the order's delivered date to the authoritative date and confirm the in/out-of-window decision; when relying on the opaque number alone, verify every plausible interpretation yields the same decision before acting.
known_bad: Reading an opaque numeric timestamp as days-since-delivery while the task also states a calendar date leads to refusing a return that is only a few days past delivery — the check fails because the days computed from the stated date are far fewer and the stated date controls.

name: Decide with an ambiguous timestamp
description: Applies when the current time is given as an opaque number with no stated unit or epoch and a deadline, window, or expiry must be checked against a calendar date.
procedure:
- Identify the event date (e.g. delivery, placement) from the record, not from the timestamp.
- List the plausible interpretations of the opaque number: day-of-year in the current year, days elapsed since the event, and days since a fixed epoch.
- Run the deadline check under every interpretation.
- If all interpretations give the same decision, proceed with that decision and say so in the reply; the ambiguity does not need resolving.
- If the interpretations disagree, prefer the reading supported by any explicit calendar date stated in the context, and say which reading was used and why.
- Compute elapsed days by counting month by month (days remaining in the first month, whole months, days in the last) rather than a single subtraction.
check: Recount the elapsed days month by month and confirm each interpretation's date lands on the same side of the deadline before trusting the decision.
known_bad: A timestamp like 45 read only as day-of-year (mid-February) when the record's event date is in late spring would report an elapsed time weeks off and could flip the window decision; the month-by-month recount and the cross-interpretation comparison expose the mismatch.

name: Register or refuse a delivered-order return
description: Applies when a customer asks to return an item from a delivered order for a refund to a chosen payment method, requiring a window, eligibility, and restocking-fee check before registering.
procedure:
- Authenticate the customer, fetch the order, and confirm its status is **delivered** and the requested item belongs to it.
- Confirm the stated reason is one of the allowed return reasons.
- Fetch the product record for the item and read its **category** from the record; do not infer the category from the item's name, which can suggest a different category than the record states.
- Compute the return window for that category from the delivery date; refuse as expired if the elapsed days exceed it.
- Refuse if the item is flagged as clearance in the product record (final sale).
- Otherwise compute the restocking fee withheld by membership tier and register the return; the refund is issued at registration.
- Accept a gift card on the customer's account as a refund destination without further conditions.
check: Before deciding, recompute the elapsed days from the delivery date shown on the order and compare against the window of the category read from the product record, and confirm the item's clearance flag from the same record.
known_bad: An item whose name sounds like electronics (e.g., a watch) but whose product record lists a 30-day category, delivered 20 days ago, would be wrongly refused as window_expired if the 14-day electronics window were assumed from the name; recomputing from the record's category passes.

name: Cancel a pending order
description: Applies when a customer asks to cancel an order that may still be in pending status and the order's total must be checked against a membership-tier cancellation threshold before deciding.
procedure:
- Authenticate the user and fetch the order; verify it belongs to the user and its status is pending.
- Compute the order total from the line items.
- Look up the user's membership tier and apply the tier's cancellation threshold: bronze $200, silver $300, gold $500. If the total exceeds the threshold, refuse with an over-threshold reason.
- Confirm the stated cancellation reason is one of the allowed ones (e.g. no longer needed, ordered by mistake); otherwise refuse.
- If all checks pass, cancel the order and refund the payment to the payment method(s) used.
check: Before finalizing, recompute the order total and re-read the user's membership tier, then verify the total is at or below the tier's threshold and the reason is allowed; only cancel if both hold.
known_bad: A pending order whose total exceeds the member's tier threshold (for example a $250 order for a bronze-tier customer, whose limit is $200) must be refused; cancelling it would fail the check.

name: Route an item-change request by order status
description: Applies when a customer asks to change an item on an order to a different variant, without stating whether the order is pending or already delivered.
procedure:
- Look up the order and read its status before choosing an operation; the customer's wording ("modify", "swap") does not determine which flow applies.
- If the order is pending, process the change as a modification of the order item, charging or refunding the price difference.
- If the order is delivered, a modification is impossible; process the change as an exchange of the delivered item for an available, non-clearance variant of the same product.
- For an exchange, confirm the delivery date falls inside the return window for the product's category, and that the new variant is available, non-clearance, and belongs to the same product.
- Compute the price difference as the new variant's price minus the returned item's price; charge or refund it via a payment method the customer has chosen and that can cover it.
- Call the exchange or modification tool with the returned item ids, new item ids, order id, and payment method id.
check: Recompute the price difference from the product catalog (new variant price minus returned item price) and compare it to the difference recorded on the order after the action; also confirm the order status now reflects the requested operation.
known_bad: An order whose recorded price difference equals the full price of the returned item instead of the gap between the two variant prices would fail this check, as would an order left in its original status with no exchange or modification recorded.

name: Refuse when restricted payment cannot cover
description: Applies when a customer requests an operation that requires them to pay a difference, but restricts payment to one specific payment method on file whose balance cannot cover the amount.
procedure:
- Recompute the amount due and compare it against the balance of the single payment method the customer authorized.
- Treat a method as declined only if the customer explicitly ruled it out or refused it; methods the customer never mentioned are not declined.
- If the authorized method cannot cover the amount, refuse the operation rather than charging any other method.
- In the refusal reply, list the other payment methods on file that would cover the amount and offer to proceed if the customer authorizes one of them.
- Never charge a method the customer declined, even if it has sufficient balance.
check: Recompute the amount due, confirm the authorized method's balance is less than that amount, and confirm the payment history or final action shows no charge to any declined method.
known_bad: A customer owes a $25 difference, authorizes a gift card with a $10 balance, and says not to use their credit card; an outcome that charges the credit card (or any unmentioned method) instead of refusing and offering alternatives fails this check.
